Christian Vision
Our Christian Vision
At Durrington Junior, our whole curriculum and learning is based upon the teaching:
"Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind. Love your neighbour as yourself." (Matthew 22: 37-39)
We live this out through our Golden Rules and School Values which encourage us to love and respect ourselves and one another. By doing this, we believe that we are being the best people we can be, and following God's commandment.
The Golden Rules are: Be Honest, Be Kind, Be Tidy, Be Helpful, Be Sensible, Be Respectful.
The School Values: TRUTH, KINDNESS & RESPECT
We hold whole school worship every Monday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday. Monday launches the theme and continues the thread through the term; Tuesday are kept for Class based Reflections on the theme for Worship that term; Wednesday is for visitors (see below); Thursday we celebrate Christianity through song; Friday is a celebration of ourselves and where we share our prayers with God.
Worship is led by staff and occasionally children, following the termly plans and using a variety of resources such as the SPCK website, Roots and Shoots, The Lion Children's Bible and the Storyteller Bible for Children.
We invite visitors to speak on a variety of themes and we have welcomed The Salvation Army, The Open the Book Team, Rev.Susan and Rev. Philip, and recently we had a Humanist speaker as well.
Parents can choose to remove their child from Collective Worship if they so wish.
Links with the Church
We are proud to be a part of the Community of All Saints Church in Durrington. Our links with the Church help us to flourish and bring our mission to the village and not just our school. The picture below is a link to the All Saints website. Click on the church.

Durrington CE VC Junior's Governors
Chair of Governors:Mr M I Hitchen Cornerways, College RoadDurringtonSalisburyTelephone: school on 01980 652237
Chair of Children's Committee: Mr Mike Hitchen
Chair of Resources Committee: Mr Dion Spencer
The Governing BodyThe Government requires that each school have a management team, a Governing Body. This body is made up of the various stakeholders that the school serves: parents, the local authority, staff or local community and for church controlled schools, the Diocese. This helps ensure the governing body has sufficient diversity of views and experience.
The Governing Body meets as a full group three times a year. There are two committees: Resources (the school budget, all issues relating to staff, buildings, grounds, lettings and infrastructure) and Children's (curriculum, pastoral and extra-curricular issues). These committees meet a few weeks prior to the meeting of the Full Governing Body.
The purpose of the Governing Body is to work with the Headteacher, staff, parents and Local Authority, to help the school provide the best possible education for the pupils. We are accountable to the stakeholders mentioned in the first paragraph for the way in which we carry out our various responsibilities and functions.The Governors are all volunteers and the current team is listed below. If you are interested in joining us and contributing to the good of the school and the local community please get in touch with me or the Headteacher.Mike Hitchen, Chair of Governors

Reading and Homework
Reading and Homework
All children will be set homework weekly. Each child's homework programme is fixed inside their Journal (Fish Book).
Homework could be Literacy and Numeracy or an activity chosen from the Homework Menu. You can see this term's Homework Menu under the curriculum tab.
All children should read at least 3 times per week as part of their homework as well as practising their spellings and table facts up to 12 x 12.
The link below is a link to past SAT papers that cover the old Levels 3 to 5 from the National Curriculum in Science, Literacy and Mathematics. They are free to view and print out and can be a good way to practice skills at home. Answer booklets are included on the site.
http://www.satstestsonline.co.uk/sto_past_papers.aspx

Special Educational Needs & Disabilities
Provision for pupils with SEND at Durrington CE Junior School is coordinated by Mrs Jessica de Vries, SENDCo (her other roles include Interim Deputy Head Teacher, Senior Mental Health Lead, SMHL and Deputy Designated Safeguarding Lead, DDSL).
Appointments with Mrs de Vries can be made via the school office.
Mrs de Vries supports staff to ensure that pupils with special educational needs or disabilities reach their potential academically, socially and emotionally.
Please use the links below to read the school SEND Information Report, our Ordinary Available Provision (OAP) with targeted and specialist provision and our SEND Policy. Each document details how we aim to meet the needs of our pupils.
